fields.TITLE: Getting Started with the Shio Universal Editor
fields.EXCERPT: Learn how to instrument your pages with data-sh-* attributes and enable inline visual editing with Viglet Shio.
fields.CONTENT:
The Shio Universal Editor brings the power of visual, in-context editing to any web page. Instead of editing content through a traditional form-based CMS interface, authors can click directly on page elements and modify them inline.

How It Works

The architecture follows the proven pattern established by Adobe's Universal Editor, adapted for Viglet Shio. The key components are:

  • Editor Shell - The Shio Console provides the editing UI with toolbar, properties panel, and device preview.
  • Editor Bridge - A lightweight JavaScript library (shio-editor.js) that runs inside your page, detects editable elements, and communicates with the shell.
  • Data Attributes - HTML attributes (data-sh-*) that mark elements as editable and link them to Shio content.

Instrumenting Your Page

Add the shio-editor.js script to your page and annotate elements with data-sh-resource, data-sh-type, and data-sh-prop attributes. The editor does the rest.
fields.AUTHOR: Alexandre Oliveira

fields.TITLE: The Future of Headless CMS: Visual Editing Meets API-First
fields.EXCERPT: How modern CMS platforms are bridging the gap between developer flexibility and author experience.
fields.CONTENT:
The headless CMS revolution promised developers freedom from monolithic architectures. But in doing so, it often left content authors stranded with bare-bones editing interfaces disconnected from the final output.

The Author Experience Gap

Traditional headless CMS platforms deliver content via APIs, which is great for developers building frontends with React, Vue, or any framework. However, authors editing content in a generic form have no visual context of how their changes will appear on the live site.

Enter the Universal Editor

The universal editor approach solves this by overlaying editing capabilities directly on the rendered page. The page is loaded in an iframe, and a thin JavaScript bridge enables the CMS to detect and modify editable regions. This gives authors a true WYSIWYG experience while preserving the headless, API-first architecture underneath.

Viglet Shio implements this pattern natively, making it one of the few open-source platforms that offers both a headless API and a visual editing experience.
fields.AUTHOR: Alexandre Oliveira

fields.TITLE: Building Components for Visual Editing
fields.EXCERPT: Best practices for creating reusable components that work seamlessly with the Shio Universal Editor.
fields.CONTENT:
When building pages that support visual editing, component design becomes critical. Each component needs to clearly expose its editable regions through data attributes while maintaining clean, semantic HTML.

Component Anatomy

A well-structured editable component has three layers:

  1. Resource - The data-sh-resource attribute identifies which content object (post) this component represents.
  2. Properties - Each editable field within the component uses data-sh-prop to map to a specific post attribute.
  3. Type - The data-sh-type attribute tells the editor how to handle editing (text, richtext, media, etc.).

Tips for Good Components

  • Keep components focused — one resource per component
  • Use semantic HTML elements that naturally contain the content type
  • Add descriptive data-sh-label values so authors know what they are editing
  • Test both with and without the editor — components should look great standalone
fields.AUTHOR: Alexandre Oliveira
